references.text: The parallel passage in Matthew where the disciples give the same answers: some say John the Baptist, others Elijah, and still others Jeremiah or one of the prophets.
The parallel passage in Mark where people think Jesus is John the Baptist, Elijah, or one of the prophets.
The parallel passage in Mark where Jesus asks his disciples who people say he is, and they answer John the Baptist, Elijah, or one of the prophets.

Herod hears about all that Jesus does, and some say that John has risen from the dead, others that Elijah has appeared, and still others that one of the old prophets has risen—the same views mentioned in verse 19.
Herod hears about Jesus' deeds and believes he is John the Baptist, who has risen from the dead, reflecting the public opinion noted in Luke 9:19.
The people say that a great prophet has arisen among them, which corresponds to the view that Jesus was one of the old prophets.
The people ask John if he is the Christ, Elijah, or the Prophet—the same categories used for Jesus in Luke 9:19.
Moses' promise that the Lord will raise up a prophet like him. The expectation of 'one of the old prophets' in Luke 9:19 is linked to this hope for the coming prophet.
The promise that Elijah will return before the day of the Lord. The public opinion that Jesus might be Elijah, as mentioned in Luke 9:19, is based on this prophecy.
